ai.description: *Nanorana arunachalensis* is a small frog (30–40 mm) with a brown-mottled dorsum and yellowish venter. It features a distinct tympanum, prominent skin folds, and lacks vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana arunachalensis* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent glandular folds on its dorsum, which are absent in other similar *Nanorana* species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana arunachalensis* inhabits high-altitude, fast-flowing rocky streams within the dense subtropical evergreen forests of Arunachal Pradesh, India.
ai.behavior: The Arunachal Cascade Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active along fast-flowing mountain streams to hunt for small invertebrates under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana arunachalensis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 150–200 eggs attached to submerged rocks in fast-flowing hill streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana arunachalensis* is endemic to the Arunachal Pradesh state in Northeast India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation streams within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The Arunachal Cascade Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes while perched on mossy rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
